title: L2-ARCTIC: a non-native English speech corpus
task: read CMU ARCTIC prompts; spontaneous suitcase-story retelling
token_or_recording_size: 26,867 read-speech recordings; 27.1 h; 3,599 manually examined read utterances; spontaneous subset from 22 speakers
annotation_target: corrected word boundaries; corrected phone boundaries; phone substitution/deletion/addition labels; annotator comments; spontaneous phonetic transcriptions
manual_scope: 3,599 read utterances manually examined; manual annotation files contain corrected word/phone boundaries and error tags; suitcase annotations produced by trained research assistants, cross-checked, then checked by a project PI
access: public corpus with form/license-gated download; public documentation directly accessible
decision_reason: Primary non-native productions with an explicitly isolated human-corrected annotation subset. Forced-alignment-only tiers are excluded rather than treated as manual.
evidence_summary: Current project documentation reports 24 speakers across six L1 groups, 26,867 utterances/27.1 h, 3,599 human-examined utterances, 14,098 substitutions, 3,420 deletions and 1,092 additions; the v5.0 suitcase corpus adds manually annotated spontaneous speech from 22 speakers.
